subsystems.name: Airframe and propulsion
subsystems.role: keeps the drone in the air and carries whatever payload it needs.

subsystems.name: Perception and navigation
subsystems.role: lets the drone know where it is and avoid obstacles.

subsystems.name: Autonomy software
subsystems.role: plans paths and carries out tasks without a human pilot.

subsystems.name: Payload and tooling
subsystems.role: what the drone actually does — a camera, a delivery winch, or a robotic arm.

subsystems.name: Communication and ground control
subsystems.role: links the drone to operators and site systems.

subsystems.name: Site data and digital twin
subsystems.role: turns drone data into useful construction information.

buildSteps.title: Define the task
buildSteps.detail: Choose whether the drone will survey, inspect, deliver or manipulate. Each task needs a different payload and level of autonomy.

buildSteps.title: Design the airframe
buildSteps.detail: Size rotors and battery for the required flight time and payload. Heavy lift needs large propellers and high-capacity batteries, which limits endurance.

buildSteps.title: Integrate perception sensors
buildSteps.detail: Mount and calibrate GNSS/RTK, cameras, LiDAR and inertial sensors so the drone can build a picture of its surroundings.

buildSteps.title: Develop the autonomy stack
buildSteps.detail: Write and test path planning, obstacle avoidance and task execution in simulation before flying real hardware.

buildSteps.title: Build the ground control and data pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Set up radio links, a ground station and software that turns drone imagery into 3D models and progress reports.

buildSteps.title: Test in a controlled site
buildSteps.detail: Fly repeated missions in an enclosed area or test site, gradually removing human oversight and measuring reliability.

buildSteps.title: Trial on a live construction site
buildSteps.detail: Work alongside workers with safety pilots and geofencing, starting with simple tasks like surveying and inspection.

buildSteps.title: Certify and scale
buildSteps.detail: Obtain regulatory approvals for beyond-visual-line-of-sight and autonomous operation, then deploy a fleet with maintenance and recharging logistics.

prerequisites.tech: Precise positioning without GNSS (indoor and under structures)
prerequisites.why: construction sites are cluttered and often lack reliable satellite signals; visual-inertial odometry is improving but not yet robust enough for all tasks.
current battery-powered drones carry only a few kilograms for 20–40 minutes; most construction materials are far heavier.

prerequisites.tech: Manipulation and grasping in unstructured environments
prerequisites.why: robotic arms on drones are lab demonstrations; they cannot yet perform construction tasks reliably or safely.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory framework for autonomous BVLOS flights
prerequisites.why: most countries require a human pilot in line of sight; rules for autonomous fleets are still emerging.
drones need a digital model of the site to plan missions and compare as-built progress.

pathway.milestone: drones used for aerial surveying, photogrammetry and visual inspections
pathway.unlocks: faster site mapping and regular progress records.

pathway.milestone: autonomous inspection flights with machine-learning defect detection
pathway.unlocks: routine structural checks without a pilot on site.

pathway.milestone: drone delivery of small tools and materials on site
pathway.unlocks: reduced walking and waiting for small items.

pathway.milestone: drones with manipulators performing simple repetitive tasks such as painting or sealing
fleets of autonomous drones coordinating logistics and construction tasks
pathway.unlocks: round-the-clock site operations with fewer workers in hazardous areas.
